summary: The change updates the project-delivery review/workflow references, the refactoring-review skill, and the delivery ledger to require committing git-ignored review run directories (`.review-benchmark/runs/`, `.agents/reviews/`) to an `llm-ledger` branch before worktree removal. Cross-references (`Checkout Isolation`, `workflow.md`) resolve correctly and the claim that both paths are git-ignored is accurate (`.gitignore:27`, `.gitignore:45`), but the new procedure omits the force-add required to stage ignored paths and never describes switching to or creating the `llm-ledger` branch, so a literal follow-through either stages nothing or lands the evidence on the delivery topic branch, defeating the change's own MUST.

findings.title: Committing git-ignored run directories requires a force-add that the procedure omits
findings.trigger: A delivery agent follows the instruction literally and stages the evidence with a plain `git add .review-benchmark/runs/ .agents/reviews/` (or `git add -A`) while preparing the `llm-ledger` commit.
findings.consequence: Git reports `The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files` and stages nothing, so the commit is empty or omits the evidence; the subsequent `git worktree remove` deletes the only copies and the review audit trail is lost, violating the change's MUST.
findings.evidence: `.gitignore:27` ignores `.review-benchmark/` and `.gitignore:45` ignores `.agents/*` (re-including only `.agents/skills/`), confirmed by `git check-ignore`; `workflow.md:20-23` instructs committing exactly those git-ignored paths with no `-f`/`--force` flag.
findings.suggestedFix: Document that the two directories must be staged with `git add -f` (or `--force`) and, ideally, that the add/commit happens from a dedicated `llm-ledger` worktree with the push verified before `git worktree remove`.

findings.title: Procedure omits the branch switch needed to commit onto `llm-ledger`
findings.trigger: The agent runs `git add -f ... && git commit` while the delivery worktree is still checked out on the topic branch, since the text says only to 'commit ... to the `llm-ledger` branch' without instructing a checkout, `--orphan` creation, or a separate worktree.
findings.consequence: The run directories are committed to the delivery topic branch and pushed with it, polluting the delivery history with raw evidence while `llm-ledger` never receives them; after `git worktree remove`, the audit trail is still gone.
findings.evidence: `workflow.md:19-22` states 'commit the delivery's review run directories ... to the `llm-ledger` branch' with no intervening branch-change step, and the delivery worktree is on the topic branch per the checkout isolation flow in `workflow.md:8-14`.
findings.suggestedFix: Spell out the sequence: create/checkout `llm-ledger` (via a dedicated `git worktree add` or `git checkout --orphan llm-ledger` when absent), copy the two run directories into that checkout, force-add and commit under the topic name, push, then return to the delivery worktree to remove it.
